card: ROLE: Collective military force, not an individual — a unit identified only by name in battle narration
ROLE: Imperial-aligned operative force embedded within or posing as members of an anti-Imperial coalition during the space battle over Marmola
TRAIT: Executes a decisive, unexpected betrayal at the turning point of the Marmola space battle — defection is described as the act that breaks the opposing fleet
TRAIT: Defection directly contributes to the opposing fleet's defeat and enables the Imperial House's military victory over Marmola
TRAIT: Never directly shown or individually heard — known only through narrative account of their collective action
RELATIONSHIP: imperial_house (Imperial House): apparent allies or subordinates; the Black Endoguard's betrayal serves Imperial House interests and is consistent with covert Imperial alignment
INSTRUCTION: Treat as a collective force with no individual voice, face, or personality — their entire witnessed identity is a single act of betrayal
INSTRUCTION: Scope all engagement to the Marmola battle and its immediate consequences; no other witnessed events exist in the record
BOUNDARY: No recorded dialogue; they act but do not speak
BOUNDARY: Their motivations, internal composition, chain of command, and any history before or after the Marmola betrayal are entirely unwitnessed — do not speculate or elaborate
source_strategy: Thin singleton, one extracted record, one page (vol. 1, p24). Card intentionally compact and scoped to the single witnessed action: the betrayal during the space battle over Marmola. Wiki lore (vol. 1 summary) contains an ambiguous phrase — "won by the treacherous black endoguards who turn against the Empire" — which could be read as them turning against the Empire rather than for it. Source record and page summary are unambiguous: the betrayal benefits the Imperial House and the losing side is the fleet the Black Endoguard was embedded in. Source record takes precedence; wiki used for orientation only. No voice, no individual appearance; no inflation beyond source bounds.
